groups.defect: Zoho Bigin passes the credential ID instead of its owner's userId to refreshOAuthTokens, causing incorrect user lookup and sync routing.
groups.rationale: All identify the same incorrect third argument. Cross-account token retrieval and inappropriate syncing of team credentials are consequences of that same mistake.

groups.defect: The team credential creation branch returns before checking administrator access.
groups.rationale: Both describe the same misplaced authorization check and propose moving it before team credential creation.

groups.defect: refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode, violating the response shapes expected by Google, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM, and HubSpot callers.
groups.rationale: These report the same shared helper return-contract defect from its definition and consuming code. The broader suggestions already enumerate the affected callers; the Google-only reports describe a subset.

groups.defect: Google Calendar saves the entire SafeParse result as credential.key instead of the parsed credential data.
groups.rationale: Every suggestion identifies the same wrapper being persisted at the same update site.

groups.defect: The minimum token schema strips token fields and the parser invents a refresh-token placeholder; Salesforce additionally refreshes and writes credentials unconditionally, rejects responses using statusText, and constructs its connection with the old access token.
groups.rationale: The parser suggestions overlap on stripped fields and placeholder refresh tokens. The Salesforce suggestion explicitly reports the same placeholder problem, linking it into the group while adding independent Salesforce defects that must survive consolidation.

groups.defect: The webhook uses a non-constant-time secret comparison and leaves malformed request bodies and decryption/parsing failures unhandled.
groups.rationale: Both report the secret-comparison defect. s_6431b4bc additionally reports missing input-error handling, which the merged comment must retain.
